'''Erwin Bolthausen''' (born 15 October 1945 in [[Rohr, Aargau]]) is a Swiss mathematician, specializing in probability theory, statistics, and stochastic models in [[mathematical physics]].

==Education and career==
Bolthausen received his doctorate in mathematics under [[Beno Eckmann]] in 1973 from [[ETH Zurich]]. Bolthausen's thesis was entitled ''Einfache Isomorphietypen in lokalisierten Kategorien und einfache Homotopietypen von Polyeder'' (Simple isomorphic types in localized categories and simple homotopy types of polyhedra).<ref>{{MathGenealogy | id = 18396 | name = Erwin Bolthausen}}</ref> In 1978 he completed his habilitation at the [[University of Konstanz]] and was then an associate professor of mathematics at the [[Goethe University Frankfurt]] for the academic year 1978–1979. From 1979 to 1990 he was a full professor at [[Technische Universität Berlin]]. Since 1990 he is a full professor at the [[University of Zurich]],<ref name=homepage>{{cite web|title=Prof. Dr. Erwin Bolthausen|website=Institut for Mathematik, Universität Zürich|url=https://www.math.uzh.ch/index.php?id=people&key1=106}} (with CV & links to many preprints)</ref> where he headed the ''Institut für Mathematik'' from 1998 to 2001.<ref name=Leopoldina/>

In the early years of his career Bolthausen did research on [[Martingale (probability theory)|martingale]] convergence theorems, combinatorial limit theorems, and the [[large deviations theory]]. Later in his career he dealt with stochastic models in mathematical physics, such as wandering in random media, phenomena related to random interfaces ([[Entropic force|entropic repulsion]], [[wetting]] phenomena), [[spin glass]]es, and [[polymer]]s in random media.

Bolthausen has been a member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] since 2007.<ref name-Leopoldina<ref name=Leopoldina>{{cite web|title=Prof. Dr. Erwin Bolthausen|website=Leopoldina Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitglieder/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/1213/}}</ref> From 1995 to 2000 he was a member of the council of the [[Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach]]. He is since 2002 a member of the scientific advisory board of the [[Saint-Flour, Cantal#École d'Eté de Probabilités|''École d'Eté de Probabilités de Saint-Flour'']] and since 1994 a member of the Board of Trustees of the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]].<ref name=homepage/>

He was an associate editor from 1987 to 1989 for the ''[[Annals of Statistics]]'' and from 1988 to 1993 for the ''[[Annals of Probability]]''. For the journal ''[[Probability Theory and Related Fields]]'' he was editor-in-chief from 1994 to 2000 and is an associate editor since 2000.<ref name=homepage/>

Bolthausen was in 2002 in [[Beijing]] an invited speaker with talk '' Localization-delocalization phenomena for random interfaces ''<ref>{{cite book|chapter=''Localization-delocalization phenomena for random interfaces'' by Erwin Bolthausen|title=Proceedings of the ICM, Beijing 2002|volume=2|pages=25–40}} [https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0304366 arXiv preprint]</ref> at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] and in 1996 in Budapest with talk ''Large deviations and perturbations of random walks and random surfaces''<ref>{{cite book|author=Bolthausen, E.|year=1998|chapter=Large deviations and perturbations of random walks and random surfaces|title=''In:'' Balog, A; Katona, G O H; Recski, A; Szász, D., eds., European Congress of Mathematics, Vol. 1 (Budapest 1996)|volume=168 |issue=168 |location=Basel|publisher=Birkhäuser|pages=108–120|url=https://www.zora.uzh.ch/id/eprint/22175/}}</ref> at the [[European Congress of Mathematicians]].
